findings.title: const_modules_over_50 counts names on from-import statements: entry_config.py reads 118 const names and counts 3

findings.mechanism: measure() builds const_fanout by summing len(node.names) over ImportFrom nodes naming .const; a read through a module binding (`from . import const`, then const.X) adds nothing. thermal_model.py is counted 67 while it reads 135 distinct names (67 imported, 75 through the binding); entry_config.py is counted 3 and reads 118. The architecture score's own planted case N4_const_namespace_import (tools/audit/archscore/planted/perturb/) labels that re-spelling NULL -- 'identical dependency, different spelling' -- so the ratchet pays a change the score calls no change.

findings.title: The clone censuses key a window by its owning function: a rule written twice in one function is not a copy
findings.claim: duplication_copies -- the score's heaviest metric (weight 8.93, counters.gapped_clones) and the ratchet's row (structure.duplicate_clones) -- counts a window only when two different functions own it, so a window written twice inside one function reads 0 in every one of the 95 package files, and folding two clone functions' bodies, both still written out, under one def reads IMPROVES.
findings.mechanism: Both censuses file each window under `windows[digest].add((rel, fn.name, fn.lineno))` and form a class only from a digest with two or more owners. Two places of one function are one owner. Today's tree holds 6 such in-function copies under the ratchet's adjacent window (m1_ratchet_census.py COPY lines: climate.extra_state_attributes 4 places, thermal_model.simulate_trajectory_batch 4, optimizer._comfort_terms_batch 3, optimizer._analyze_forecast_trajectory 2, tariff._smooth_topk_sum 2, tariff._smooth_topk_sum_batch 2) and 15 under the score's gapped window (duplication_copies 18 -> 33 with the owner keyed by place), none priced. The same rule is a game: prototype `fold` moves ledger.add's and ledger.observe_meta_mean's bodies verbatim into the two branches of one `_fold`, shares nothing, and reads dS +0.6964 IMPROVES, admissible (duplication_copies 18 -> 17). No red-team attempt under tools/audit/archscore/planted/redteam/ plants it.

findings.title: Seven pure modules reach Home Assistant through an import they do not need: layer_violations 13 -> 6
findings.claim: Seven of the 13 layer violations the score counts ride on imports with a pure owner: comfort_learning.py, external_heat.py and power_guard.py take utc_elapsed_seconds through accuracy.py's re-export although drift.py owns it; tariff.py takes the constant HISTORY_LENGTH from accuracy.py, which carries optimizer.py and topology.py with it; and grid_fee.py reaches the glue through currency.py, whose only Home Assistant import is one annotation. Two prototypes read layer_violations 13 -> 6, dS +1.0000, admissible; the six left need a design.
findings.mechanism: layering.py ranks a module by the highest boundary it imports itself (pure < scipy < Home Assistant) and counts a module reaching a higher layer through package imports. m7_layer_edges.py names the carrier edge of each violation: 11 of the 13 have exactly one. accuracy.py imports homeassistant.util.dt at module level and carries five edges (comfort_learning, external_heat, power_guard, sysid, tariff); tariff carries optimizer's and topology's. accuracy.py:43 already re-exports utc_elapsed_seconds from drift; eleven modules import it from drift and eight still from accuracy. HISTORY_LENGTH (accuracy.py:51) is a number the tariff's house-sample cap also reads. currency.py imports homeassistant.core.HomeAssistant for the annotation of resolve_currency alone, under `from __future__ import annotations`. NEEDING A DESIGN, not built: disinfection, price_model, quiet_windows and sysid ride on inputs.py, which is glue by one function-scope import of the clock (inputs.py:984) that the suite freezes -- the pure helpers leave the module or the reader's clock is injected (--cut inputs reads 10, --cut inputs,accuracy 3); setpoint_check rides on inputs and on issues.py, real glue; snapshots rides on store.admitted, whose domain table lives in the storage module (--cut store reads 14, not fewer).
